prerequisites: Prior knowledge of Television and Broadcasting, Radiofrequency and Microwave Technologies, Mobile Communications, Signal Processing, Terrestrial and Satellite Radiocommunications, Telecommunication Systems, Propagation and Radiation.
Solid foundation in signal processing, radiation, and radiopropagation.
For activities in English, B2 level certification (or equivalent) is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Read, draft, and prepare documentation in English on a scientific-technical topic within the field of study.
Deliver a presentation in English on a scientific-technical work within the field of study.
Associate technical specifications with transmission and reception topologies as well as their constituent subsystems.
Understand and apply the fundamental principles of radiodetermination.
Program applications for navigation and localization simulation.
Identify and select circuits and subsystems for radiodetermination systems.

syllabus_topics: 2.1.1. Positioning based on Time of Arrival (ToA / ToF).
2.1.2. Positioning based on Angle of Arrival (AoA).
2.1.3. Positioning based on Doppler velocity measurement.
2.2.3. Approach and landing aids (ILS, MLS, LAAS).
2.3.4. Enhanced precision GNSS: SBAS, RTK, PPP.
teaching_methods: Laboratory practices (group work, simulations, measurements, critical analysis)

assessment_methods.method: Final written exam (theoretical, theoretical-practical questions, exercises and problems)
Continuous assessment: Laboratory work (presential and non-presential, reports, questionnaires, public presentations)
Continuous assessment: Delivery of proposed exercises and assignments

assessment_rules: In the ordinary sitting, a final written exam accounts for 60% of the grade, and continuous assessment accounts for 40%. Continuous assessment includes 30% for laboratory work and 10% for assignments, with 7.5% of the continuous assessment grade from English language activities. A minimum score of 4.5/10 on the final exam is required to pass the subject; if this minimum is not met, the final grade will be the lesser of 4.9 and the weighted average. In the extraordinary sitting, the exam accounts for 70% of the final grade, and the continuous assessment grade from the semester is retained for the remaining 30%. The same minimum exam score of 4.5/10 applies for passing in the extraordinary sitting.
